rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to fear God intensifies the exhortation, like repeating ‘hurry’ for emphasis.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا التكرير وجوه : الأول : تأكيد الأمر والحث عليه كقولك للرجل : اعجل اعجل فيكون أبلغ من قولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first command follows God's benefaction in creating people; the second follows their habit of invoking God when requesting things from one another.
rows.anchor: أمر بالتقوى في الأول لمكان الانعام بالخلق وغيره ، وفي الثاني أمر بالتقوى لمكان وقوع التساؤل به فيما يلتمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Rabb evokes nurturing and beneficence, inviting obedience; calling Him Allah evokes majesty and awe, warning against disobedience and punishment.
rows.anchor: والرب لفظ يدل على التربية والاحسان ، والاله لفظ يدل على القهر والهيبة ، فأمرهم بالتقوى بناء على الترغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking by God means invoking Him to strengthen a request, appeal, oath, or plea for another's help and support.
rows.anchor: بالله أسألك ، وبالله أشفع اليك ، وبالله أحلف عليك ، إلى غير ذلك مما يؤكد المرء به مراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza's genitive reading is clear: Arabs customarily appealed to kinship as well as God, and polytheists even wrote the Prophet invoking both.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة حمزة فهي ظاهرة من حيث المعنى ، والتقدير : واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the accusative reading, the phrase means ‘fear God and fear kinship,’ understood as maintaining family ties rather than cutting them.
rows.anchor: وأما القراءة بالنصب فالمعنى يرجع إلى ذلك ، والتقدير : واتقوا الله واتقوا الأرحام

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi argues that the accusative reading shows one expression can carry different meanings: fearing God means obeying Him, while fearing kin means keeping ties through kindness.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : وهذا أحد ما يدل على أنه قد يراد باللفظ الواحد المعاني المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He answers that God may have uttered this expression twice, once for each distinct meaning, removing the difficulty.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يجاب عنه بأنه تعالى لعله تكلم بهذه اللفظة مرتين ، وعلى هذا التقدير يزول الاشكال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some derive rahim from rahma, meaning benefaction, and explain that kinship prompts people to show mercy to one another; they cite a divine hadith linking the names.
rows.anchor: اسم الرحم مشتق من الرحمة التي هي النعمة ، واحتج بما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others derive the word rahim from the womb, where benefaction takes place.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل اسم الرحم مشتق من الرحم الذي عنده يقع الانعام وانه الأصل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A third view makes each of the two words an independent root; al-Razi considers this kind of dispute minor.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل كل واحد منهما أصل بنفسه ، والنزاع في مثل هذا قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that it is permissible to ask someone by God.
rows.anchor: دلت الآية على جواز المسألة بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Mujahid reports from ʿUmar that the Prophet said to give to anyone who asks by God.
rows.anchor: روى مجاهد عن عمر قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( من سألكم بالله فأعطوه )

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib reports that the Prophet ordered seven things, including honoring an oath.
rows.anchor: وعن البراء بن عازب قال : أمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بسبع : منها ابرار القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning kinship magnifies its rights and reinforces the prohibition on severing it; the cited verses command against cutting ties and enjoin kindness to relatives.
rows.anchor: دل قوله تعالى : { والارحام } على تعظيم حق الرحم وتأكيد النهي عن قطعها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes the term illa in 9:8 to mean kinship.
rows.anchor: قيل في الأول : إنه القرابة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf reports a divine hadith: God is al-Raḥmān and kinship is al-raḥim; whoever connects it is connected by God, and whoever cuts it is cut off.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الرحمن بن عوف : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( يقول الله تعالى أنا الرحمن وهي الرحم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that prompt reward follows kinship ties, while prompt punishment follows transgression and a false oath.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ما من شيء أطيع الله فيه أعجل ثوابا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Anas reports that charity and kinship increase lifespan, avert an evil death, and ward off harm and disliked events.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( ان الصدقة وصلة الرحم يزيد الله بهما في العمر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet calls giving charity to a hostile relative the best charity; an unnamed interpretation says al-kāshiḥ means an enemy.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( أفضل الصدقة على ذي الرحم الكاشح ) قيل الكاشح العدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an and Sunna establish the duty to maintain kinship and the reward for doing so.
rows.anchor: فثبت بدلالة الكتاب والسنة وجوب صلة الرحم واستحقاق الثواب بها

rows.speaker: أصحاب أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: Hanafi jurists infer that owning a prohibited close relative emancipates that relative: continued service would cause estrangement and sever kinship, which is forbidden.
rows.anchor: أن الرجل اذا ملك ذا رحم محرم عتق عليه مثل الأخ والاخت ، والعم والخال

rows.speaker: أصحاب أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: Hanafi jurists also hold that a gift to a prohibited close relative cannot be reclaimed, since revocation would cause estrangement and break kinship.
rows.anchor: أن الهبة لذي الرحم المحرم لا يجوز الرجوع فيها لان ذلك الرجوع ايحاش يورث قطيعة الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names fourteen forbidden categories: seven through blood relationship, and seven otherwise—foster mothers and sisters, wives' mothers, consummated wives' daughters, sons' wives, fathers' wives (in the prior verse), and combining two sisters.
rows.anchor: نص على تحريم أربعة عشر صنفا من النسوان : سبعة منهن من جهة النسب

rows.speaker: الكرخي
rows.claim: Al-Karkhī calls the verse ambiguous because prohibition is attached to persons rather than an explicitly named act, and no act is stated as its object.
rows.anchor: ذهب الكرخي إلى أن هذه الآية مجملة قال : لأنه أضيف التحريم فيها إلى الأمهات والبنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects the ambiguity claim: the preceding prohibition of marrying fathers' former wives (4:22) makes marriage the intended prohibited act here.
rows.anchor: أن تقديم قوله تعالى : { ولا تنكحوا ما نكح ءاباؤكم } ( النساء : 22 ) يدل على أن المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary usage and necessary religious knowledge identify the prohibited act when permission or prohibition is attached to persons: eating carrion and blood, marrying mothers and daughters, and shedding a Muslim's blood.
rows.anchor: الأصل فيه أن الحرمة والاباحة إذا أضيفتا إلى الاعيان ، فالمراد تحريم الفعل المطلوب منها في العرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the clause is passive, it does not expressly name God as the agent of prohibition; that must be supplied by consensus, so the verse alone proves nothing further.
rows.anchor: أن قوله : { حرمت عليكم } مذكور على ما لم يسم فاعله ، فليس فيه تصريح بأن فاعل هذا التحريم هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording does not specify that the prohibition lasts forever; permanence requires evidence beyond the verse's apparent wording.
rows.anchor: أن قوله : { حرمت عليكم } ليس نصا في ثبوت التحريم على سبيل التأييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As direct address, the wording appears limited to those present, so applying the rule to everyone requires separate evidence.
rows.anchor: أن قوله : { حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم } خطاب مشافهة فيخصص بأولئك الحاضرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a past-tense report, the wording does not itself cover the present or future; that extension needs separate evidence.
rows.anchor: قوله : { حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم } إخبار عن ثبوت هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural wording superficially says each person is forbidden every mother and daughter, whereas the intended distributive sense pairs each person with his own mother and daughter.
rows.anchor: ظاهر قوله : { حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم } يقتضي أنه قد حرم على كل أحد جميع أمهاتهم وجميع بناتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past form suggests a new prohibition after prior permissibility; if these relations had always been forbidden, it would imply re-creating an existing prohibition, so separate evidence is needed.
rows.anchor: أن قوله : { حرمات } يشعر ظاهره بسبق الحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mothers and daughters have been forbidden from Adam's time onward in every revealed religion; Zoroaster, whom most Muslims considered a liar, reportedly allowed them.
rows.anchor: حرمة الأمهات والبنات كانت ثابتة من زمن آدم عليه السلام إلى هذا الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sister marriage was reportedly permitted in Adam's time as a necessity.
rows.anchor: أما نكاح الاخوات فقد نقل أن ذلك كان مباحا في زمن آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: بعض المشايخ
rows.claim: Some shaykhs deny that Adam's children married their sisters and say God sent houris from Paradise to marry his sons.
rows.anchor: ورأيت بعض المشايخ أنكر ذلك ، وقال : انه تعالى كان يبعث الحواري من الجنة ليزوج بهن أبناء آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi calls that account implausible: if their wives and their daughters' husbands came from Paradise, Adam's descendants would not be exclusively his children, contrary to consensus.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعيد ، لأنه إذا كان زوجات أبنائه وأزواج بناته من أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercourse is degrading: people are ashamed to mention it, do it in seclusion, and use it in many insults; mothers deserve protection because their benefaction to children is greatest.
rows.anchor: أن الوطء إذلال وإهانة ، فان الانسان يستحي من ذكره ولا يقدم عليه إلا في الموضع الخالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A daughter is part of a person, as the Prophet says of Fāṭima, so intercourse with her is likewise degrading and she must be protected.
rows.anchor: والبنت بمنزلة جزء من الانسان وبعض منه ، قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( فاطمة بضعة مني )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains that ummāt is a plural of umm, whose original form was ummah; the hāʾ was dropped in the singular.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : الأمهات جمع الأم والأم في الأصل أمهة فأسقط الهاء في التوحيد

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: A cited line uses the plural ummahāt and names Khindif as the poet's mother and Iyās as his father.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : أمهتى خندف والياس أبي

rows.speaker: الراعي
rows.claim: Al-Rāʿī's verse uses ummāt for animal mothers, illustrating that this plural is especially common for nonhuman animals.
rows.anchor: كانت نجائب منذر ومحرق أماتهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mother includes every woman in one's birth ancestry, through one or more generations and through either female or male links.
rows.anchor: كل امرأة رجع نسبك اليها بالولادة من جهة أبيك أو من جهة أمك بدرجة أو بدرجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If umm is a univocal term shared literally by one's immediate mother and all grandmothers, the verse explicitly prohibits marrying both.
rows.anchor: فان كان لفظ الأم حقيقة في الأم الأصلية وفي الجدات ، فاما أن يكون لفظا متواطئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If umm is homonymous for mother and grandmother, those who allow one shared expression to carry both senses make the verse explicit about prohibiting all grandmothers too.
rows.anchor: فمن جوزه حمل اللفظ ههنا على الكل ، وحينئذ يكون تحريم الجدات منصوصا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who forbid using a homonym for both senses either take the verse to mean only the immediate mother, leaving grandmother prohibition to consensus, or posit two divine utterances with distinct senses.
rows.anchor: فتحريم نكاحها مستفاد من هذا الوجه ، وأما تحريم نكاح الجدات فغير مستفاد من هذا النص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same interpretive options apply if the word is literal for the immediate mother but metaphorical for grandmothers, since one word cannot simultaneously carry its literal and figurative senses.
rows.anchor: ثبت أنه لا يجوز استعمال اللفظ الواحد دفعة واحدة في حقيقته ومجازه معا

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires the legal penalty for a man who marries and consummates marriage with his mother; Abū Ḥanīfa does not.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رحمه الله : إذا تزوج الرجل بأمه ودخل بها يلزمه الحد ، وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله لا يلزمه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that such a marriage is void and the intercourse is therefore unqualified zinā, requiring the penalty in 24:2; its offer and acceptance cannot form a valid contract, and scripture categorically invalidates it.
rows.anchor: حجة الشافعي أن وجود هذا النكاح وعدمه بمثابة واحدة ، فكان هذا الوطء زنا محضا فيلزمه الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A daughter is every female descended from a person by birth through one or more generations, through either female or male links.
rows.anchor: كل أنثى يرجع نسبها اليك بالولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether a son's or daughter's daughter is literally or figuratively called a daughter is the same lexical question discussed for grandmothers.
rows.anchor: وأما بنت الابن وبنت البنت فهل تسمى بنتا حقيقة أو مجازا ؟ فالبحث فيه عين ما ذكرناه في الأمهات

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that a daughter conceived through fornication is not forbidden to the fornicator; Abū Ḥanīfa holds that she is.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رحمه الله : البنت المخلوقة من ماء الزنا لا تحرم على الزاني . وقال أبو حنيفة : تحرم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that biological conception cannot establish paternity consistently under Abū Ḥanīfa's rules: a child of a purchased virgin may lack paternity, while a child of distant spouses has it despite no biological conception by the husband.
rows.anchor: الأول : أن أبا حنيفة إما أن يثبت كونها بنتا له بناء على الحقيقة ، وهي كونها مخلوقة من مائه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that legal lineage from adultery is denied by Muslim consensus, and a judge would have to prevent the child from claiming the fornicator as her father.
rows.anchor: أجمع المسلمون على أنه لا نسب لولد الزنا من الزاني ، ولو انتسب إلى الزاني لوجب على القاضي منعه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī cites the Prophet's rule that a child belongs to the marital bed and the adulterer receives the stone, restricting lineage to the marriage bed.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثاني : التمسك بقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( الولد للفراش وللعاهر الحجر )

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī infers she is not his daughter because she inherits (4:11), could be subject to his marriage guardianship, and would be owed maintenance and custody; none applies, and solitude with her would be permitted.
rows.anchor: لو كانت بنتا له لأخذت الميراث لقوله تعالى : { للذكر مثل حظ الانثيين } ( النساء : 11 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since she is not his daughter and fornication does not create affinity prohibition either, she is not forbidden to marry him.
rows.anchor: فثبت أنها غير محرمة على الزاني والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forbidden sisters include full sisters, paternal half-sisters, and maternal half-sisters.
rows.anchor: ويدخل فيه الأخوات من الأب والأم معا

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī defines a paternal aunt as the sister of any male ancestor, including a mother's father's sister; a maternal aunt is a sister of any female ancestor, including a father's mother's sister.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : كل ذكر رجع نسبك اليه فأخته عمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nieces through brothers and sisters follow the same rule as daughters descended directly from oneself.
rows.anchor: والقول في بنات الأخ وبنات الأخت كالقول في بنات الصلب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The seven blood-relationship categories are expressly prohibited and, according to the commentators, can never become lawful.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : كل امرأة حرم الله نكاحها للنسب والرحم ، فتحريمها مؤبد لا يحل بوجه من الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rest of the verse names women who would otherwise be lawful but become prohibited through a temporary circumstance.
rows.anchor: وأما اللواتي يحل نكاحهن ثم يصرن محرمات بسبب طارىء ، فهن اللاتي ذكرن في باقي الآية

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says wet nurses are called mothers because they create a prohibition, just as the Prophet's wives are called the believers' mothers because of their protected status (33:6).
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : المرضعات سماهن أمهات لأجل الحرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse expressly names foster mothers and sisters, the Prophet's rule extends the prohibition of nursing to every relation forbidden by blood kinship.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى نص في هذه الآية على حرمة الأمهات والأخوات من جهة الرضاعة إلا أن الحرمة غير مقصورة عليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming a nursing mother and sister signals that nursing follows lineage: of seven blood-prohibited classes, two arise through birth and five through sibling relationships; the verse names one example from each group, and the hadith confirms the inference.
rows.anchor: لما سمى المرضعة أما ، والمرضعة أختا ، فقد نبه بذلك على أنه تعالى أجرى الرضاع مجرى النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A milk-mother is the woman who nursed someone and any woman maternally related to her through birth or nursing; the same applies to the milk-father and the descendants treated as daughters.
rows.anchor: أم الأنسان من الرضاع هي التي أرضعته ، وكذلك كل امرأة انتسبت إلى تلك المرضعة بالأمومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A full foster sister shares both milk parents: she is a stranger nursed by one's mother with one's father's milk, whether nursed at the same time or before or after.
rows.anchor: وهي الصغيرة الأجنبية التي أرضعتها أمك بلبن أبيك ، سواء أرضعتها معك أو مع ولد قبلك أو بعدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A paternal foster sister shares one's father but not one's mother: one's father's wife nursed her with his milk.
rows.anchor: وهي التي أرضعتها زوجة أبيك بلبن أبيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A maternal foster sister shares one's mother but not one's father: one's mother nursed her with another man's milk.
rows.anchor: وهي التي أرضعتها أمك بلبن رجل آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once foster parents are defined, the same method identifies foster aunts, uncles, nieces, and nephews.
rows.anchor: واذا عرفت ذلك سهل عليك معرفة العمات والخالات وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires five nursing sessions for prohibition; Abū Ḥanīfa considers even one session sufficient.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رحمة الله عليه : الرضاع يحرم بشرط أن يكون خمس رضعات ، وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه : الرضعة الواحدة كافية

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī argues that the verse ties maternal or sibling status to nursing, so any occurrence of nursing should trigger the ruling.
rows.anchor: واحتج أبو بكر الرازي بهذه الآية فقال : انه تعالى علق هذا الاسم يعني الأمومة والاخوة بفعل الرضاع

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
rows.claim: He answers an objection that ‘mothers who clothed you’ would imply prior motherhood: nursing itself confers the maternal name, unlike clothing.
rows.anchor: الرضاع هو الذي يكسوها سمة الأمومة ، فلما كان الاسم مستحقا بوجود الرضاع كان الحكم معلقا به

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: When told that Ibn al-Zubayr allowed one or two feeds, Ibn ʿUmar answered that God's ruling is better and cited foster sisters, understanding the verse to prohibit even little nursing.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عمر : قضاء الله خير من قضاء ابن الزبير ، قال الله تعالى : { وأخواتكم من الرضاعة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi calls Abū Bakr's argument circular: whether motherhood arises after one or five feeds is the disputed issue, so using this verse to assume it follows any nursing begs the question.
rows.anchor: وهل النزاع الا فيه ، فان عندي أن اسم الأمومة إنما جاء من الرضاع خمس مرات ، وعندك إنما جاء من أصل الرضاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar's reading is countered by Ibn al-Zubayr's opposite reading; because both were learned Companions and Arabic speakers, one cannot count one as proof while excluding the other.
rows.anchor: فهو معارض بما أن ابن الزبير ما فهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says only extreme partisanship that blinds the heart could hide the weakness in these arguments.
rows.anchor: ولولا التعصب الشديد المعمي للقلب لما خفي ضعف هذه الكلمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī then relied on hadith and analogy, but al-Razi says a Qur'anic legal discussion should derive only from the verse; other proofs belong in jurisprudence books.
rows.anchor: ومن تكلم في أحكام القرآن وجب أن لا يذكر إلا ما يتسنبطه من الآية ، فأما ما سوى ذلك فانما يليق بكتب الفقه
